title: Priority-based fallback and hedging strategy for downstream resilience
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We continue to see sporadic tail latency and request drops when downstream dependencies (Redis/Kafka/Postgres) experience regional blips or transient overload. Current single-hop retry logic and large shared connection pools sometimes amplify failure domains. Goal: Implement a priority-based fallback + hedging pattern that interoperates with connection pool limits, SLO-aware throttling, and multi-region routing so user-facing SLOs remain protected while minimizing cost and correctness regressions.

Success criteria: 
- 99.9th percentile end-to-end latency improves by >= 20% under injected downstream load in staged canary.
- Error rate (5xx) attributable to dependency timeouts reduced by >= 50% for routed traffic.
- No data loss for Kafka at-least-once paths; clear post-deploy validation steps.
- Rollout with automated gradual ramp and observability (dashboards + synthetic checks) in place.

Approach overview: 
1) Priority tagging: Requests carry a service-priority marker (P0/P1/P2) set by caller (inference, embeddings, eval pipelines). Platform will enforce different degradation strategies per priority.
2) Fast hedging layer: For P0 requests, issue parallel hedged read to a secondary replica (within region or cross-region depending on latency) if primary read exceeds hedging threshold (e.g., 60ms). Cancel slower response on arrival. Hedging threshold and replication choices driven by region/latency profiles.
3) Graceful fallback policies: Define ordered fallback chain per dependency: primary -> local read-replica -> region-fallback cache -> degraded synthetic response (for non-critical requests). Each step has configurable time budgets and counters for circuit-breaker trips.
4) SLO-aware shedding: When upstream queueing/conn-pool saturation detected, shed P2 (best-effort) traffic first, then P1, protecting P0 while maintaining global throughput targets. Shedding decisions use real-time SLO burn-rate and token-bucket smoothing.
5) Connection-pool tuning: Implement soft per-priority pool reservations and an emergency fast-path that bypasses long blocking waits by returning a controlled error or degraded placeholder to callers, preventing global pool exhaustion.
6) Observability & runbooks: New dashboards for per-priority latency, hedging hit-rate, circuit-breaker state, and downstream RTT distributions. Auto-escalation playbooks for repeated cross-region failures.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Increased traffic due to hedging: cap hedged requests with adaptive sampling and only enable for P0; monitor token usage and add budget-based throttles.
- Consistency hazards for writes: Writes will not be hedged; instead route to leader and use retry-with-idempotency-key patterns. Document this clearly for SDKs.
- Cost/regulatory concerns for cross-region fallback: Provide configuration flags per customer to disable cross-region hedging or restrict to specific regions.

Rollout plan: 
- Phase 1 (staging): Implement feature flags + simulate hedging in staging with synthetic load (2/15 - 2/28).
- Phase 2 (canary): Enable P0 hedging for 5% of traffic in us-west with read-only workloads and monitor (3/01 - 3/10).
- Phase 3 (gradual ramp): Expand to additional regions and gradually include P1 with stricter budgets (3/11 - 3/30).
- Phase 4 (GA): Enable as opt-in customer feature with defaults guarded by tenant-level config (runtime-1.24 window).

Telemetry to add: hedged_request_count, hedged_hit_rate, fallback_step_counter, pool_wait_time_histogram per-priority, slo_burn_rate, shed_rate_by_priority.

Operational notes: Create a dedicated alert when hedged_hit_rate > 10% and pool_wait_time 95p > SLO threshold; this indicates upstream instability requiring immediate investigation.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Initial triage: engineering, infra, and product aligned on priority tagging approach. Action: Aisha to draft proto for priority headers and SDK changes.
2025-02-14 - Design review: Sofia Martínez (Design) reviewed UX impacts for Console toggles and suggested exposing hedging metrics in route-level dashboards. Added label 'console-metrics'.

2025-02-18 - Spike complete: Liam ran a microbenchmark with 1000 RPS, injected 200ms tail at Redis; observed 27% reduction in p99 latency for hedged reads but hedging increased total token count by 6%. Results: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/72

2025-02-21 - Architecture sync: Decided not to hedge writes. For reads, hedging defaults to intra-region replica; cross-region allowed under tenant opt-in. Evan Ross requested an explicit cost-metering event when cross-region hedging occurs.

2025-02-25 - PR opened for runtime changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/523 (implements hedging timeout, priority headers, pool reservation). Assigned reviewers: Priya Rao, Miguel Ortiz.

2025-03-01 - Canary started: 5% P0 traffic in us-west. Early metrics: hedged_hit_rate=4.8%, p99 latency improvement ~18%, hedging budget under cap. Observability dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abc123/hedging-overview

2025-03-02 - QA note: Integration tests flagged a rare cancellation race when hedged replica and primary both respond near-simultaneously; fix proposal in PR review comments (use token-cancel ordering).
2025-03-02 - Next steps: Finish race-condition fix, add unit tests for pool reservation, and prepare canary expansion checklist with playbook entries for rollback and escalation.
